content:
pat: FYI a customer using Wrangler + esbuild hit breakage when bundling our SDK for Cloudflare Workers. Error: `Uncaught ReferenceError: process is not defined` at startup.
eli: did they use the default wrangler config? sometimes wrangler adds node polyfills depending on target.
pat: minimal repro: `import {createClient} from '@redwood/inference'` in a Worker, `wrangler dev` -> runtime throws. Build output references `process.env` checks and `require('buffer')`.
jon: sounds like our main entry leaks Node checks. We ship browser build but it still contains a tiny `require('buffer')` via crypto helper.
sasha: the crypto helper uses `randomBytes` from `crypto` and falls back to `require('buffer')` to create a Buffer. Workers don't have Buffer.
pat: customer tried `define: { 'process.env.NODE_ENV': '"production"' }` in esbuild which removed some branches but still failed.
eli: common approaches: 1) publish an explicit `exports` map with `"./edge"` entry pointing to a pure ESM worker build; 2) ship a small `edge.ts` shim that only uses `globalThis.crypto` and `TextEncoder`; 3) adjust typings to avoid `NodeJS` libs.
jon: typings are annoying: our `index.d.ts` imports `Stream`/`Buffer` types which pull `lib.dom` vs `lib.node` conflicts. Workers TS projects usually set `lib: ["WebWorker","DOM.Iterable"]`. We need an `edge.d.ts` that uses `ArrayBuffer`/`ReadableStream` instead of Node types.
sasha: implementation notes: replace `crypto.randomBytes(16)` with `getRandomBytes(16)` helper: `if (typeof globalThis?.crypto?.getRandomValues === 'function') { const arr = new Uint8Array(n); crypto.getRandomValues(arr); return arr; } else { return nodeRandomBytes(n) }`. Avoid Buffer entirely by encoding with `TextEncoder` and using `Uint8Array`.
pat: bundler quirks: Rollup + @rollup/plugin-node-resolve + builtins plugin can accidentally polyfill Buffer. For worker-safe bundle we should set `browser: true` and prefer the edge entry so bundlers pick it. Also add `sideEffects: false` where possible to help tree-shaking.
eli: CI action: add a Miniflare-based smoke test that does `import('@redwood/inference/edge').then(c => c.createEdgeClient({apiKey: 'x'}))` in a worker context. That will catch regressions where package exports fall back to node code.
ci-bot: queued job `edge-wrangler-smoke` added to pipeline.
jon: runtime warning idea: if `typeof process === 'undefined' && typeof globalThis.Buffer === 'undefined'` then in development prints a small console.warn when the node-ish code path is detected (but compute that without referencing process directly). Use `typeof process !== 'undefined' && process?.env`.
sasha: packaging: update package.json: add `exports: {"./package.json": "./package.json", ".": {"import":"./dist/esm/index.js","require":"./dist/cjs/index.js","edge":"./dist/edge/index.js"}}` and set `types` to `./dist/esm/index.d.ts` with a `./dist/edge/index.d.ts` for conditional types with a `typesVersions` or include `./edge` path.
pat: customer workaround for now: build with esbuild target `es2020`, add plugin to replace `require('buffer')` with a lightweight Uint8Array polyfill, and add `define: { 'globalThis.Buffer': 'undefined' }` so runtime doesn't assume Buffer exists. Not ideal.
eli: small DX note: update our quickstart docs to show `import { createEdgeClient } from '@redwood/inference/edge'` and call out the runtime guarantees (no Node APIs, `fetch`/`crypto.subtle` required). Also include a short `wrangler` config snippet.
ci-bot: `edge-wrangler-smoke` started  step 2/4 complete.
jon: will file GH issue for types + packaging and assign to eng team. can someone pick the edge shim + miniflare test?
pat: i'll pick the shim and docs. ETA 2 business days.
sasha: i'll take the types cleanup and CI test wiring.
eli: thanks — i'll send a short support reply for the customer linking the workaround and ETA.
ci-bot: created issue #4190 and linked pipeline job.
